boards.title: Your First Weekend at Manhattan University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-stakes first-weekend sequence: orient yourself on campus, share a meal, try a campus activity, and make a nearby outdoor plan.

cards.title: Start with a Quad lap
cards.subtitle: Campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Walk the Quadrangle first and use the campus map to place the library, commons, academic buildings, and nearby routes before making any other plans.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor reference point for your first campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University’s campus map lists the Quadrangle as a campus space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow current university access and safety guidance.

cards.title: Find O’Malley Library
cards.subtitle: Campus navigation stop
cards.notes: Locate O’Malley Library early, then save its position on your map so you have a reliable meeting point and study destination for the week ahead.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark worth locating on day one.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University’s campus map lists O’Malley Library.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current visitor and building-access policies before entering.

cards.title: Meet at Kelly Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus gathering stop
cards.notes: Use Kelly Commons for a simple first meetup: choose a public seating area, compare schedules, and decide which campus resource or event to try next.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed campus commons with multiple dining locations.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University identifies Kelly Commons as a campus building and lists several dining locations there.
cards.access_notes: Dining and seating availability may vary; check current building access and dining information.

cards.title: Share a meal at Locke’s Loft
cards.subtitle: Campus dining stop
cards.notes: If you have an applicable meal plan or funds, meet for a meal at Locke’s Loft and use the time to trade class schedules and weekend ideas.
cards.short_summary: The university identifies Locke’s Loft as its main dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University describes Locke’s Loft Dining Hall as its main, all-you-care-to-eat buffet-style dining hall.
cards.access_notes: A meal plan, Dining Dollars, or other payment may be required; verify current hours and access before going.

cards.entity_name: Chapel of De La Salle and His Brothers
cards.title: Locate the Chapel
cards.subtitle: Quiet campus landmark
cards.notes: Add the Chapel of De La Salle and His Brothers to your campus walk, then pause outside or visit only when the building is open and its use permits.
cards.short_summary: A named chapel shown on the official campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University’s campus map lists the Chapel of De La Salle and His Brothers in Squeri Hall/Smith Auditorium.
cards.access_notes: Observe posted access rules and any worship, event, or quiet-use restrictions.

cards.title: Try the Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Student Commons, third floor
cards.notes: Bring your active Manhattan University ID and take a brief equipment-orientation visit, choosing a comfortable cardio or strength option rather than overplanning a workout.
cards.short_summary: A student-ID-accessible fitness facility in the Student Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fitness Center is on the third floor of the Student Commons and is free for Manhattan University students with an active ID card.
cards.access_notes: Active Manhattan University ID required. Published weekend hours are 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm changes before visiting.

cards.title: Check an intramural option
cards.subtitle: Recreation activity
cards.notes: Look over current intramural registration and choose a format that fits your comfort level; you can form a team or register as a free agent to be placed.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation route for trying organized play.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University says all students may join intramural sports, create a team, or enter as a free agent; games are held in Draddy Gym or Gaelic Park.
cards.access_notes: Registration and schedules are handled through IMLeagues; verify the current season before attending.

cards.title: Find Draddy Gymnasium
cards.subtitle: Athletics landmark
cards.notes: Walk by Draddy Gymnasium and note its position relative to the Quad and dining areas, so you can recognize it when an athletic or recreation plan comes up.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic facility on the official campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University’s campus map lists Draddy Gymnasium as an athletics facility.
cards.access_notes: Entry and event attendance depend on current facility and event policies.

cards.title: Walk over to Gaelic Park
cards.subtitle: Campus athletics destination
cards.notes: Use the official map to find Gaelic Park, then make it a daylight walking destination with friends and check whether any current campus activity is scheduled there.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed athletic destination near the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University’s campus map lists Gaelic Park and the Gaelic Park Athletic Center.
cards.access_notes: Use public routes and follow posted facility access rules; event access may vary.

cards.title: Ask about recreation events
cards.subtitle: Office of Student Engagement activity
cards.notes: Check the current recreation calendar or ask Student Engagement about a low-pressure activity; the program includes intramurals, tournaments, and recurring annual events.
cards.short_summary: A free student recreation program with several participation formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Manhattan University states that recreation activities and events are open to all students and have no cost for students to participate.
cards.access_notes: Open to students; consult current recreation communications for the specific event, location, and registration details.
